# [TASK] Map validation and business errors to correct statuses on both REST and gRPC

## Task

`GlobalExceptionHandler` has no handler for `MethodArgumentNotValidException`, so a request that fails bean validation on a `@Valid @RequestBody` falls through to the catch-all `Exception` handler and returns **500 with no field detail** instead of 400. The same applies to `HttpMessageNotReadableException` (malformed JSON), `MissingServletRequestParameterException` (a required query param omitted), and `MaxUploadSizeExceededException` (an upload over Spring Boot's default limit, which `application.yml` never overrides). user-service's handler — which this class's Javadoc says it mirrors — already covers the first of these.

The gRPC transport has the mirror-image gap. `AiGrpcService` builds the service-layer DTOs itself, so nothing validates them, and it catches nothing the services throw — a `ResourceNotFoundException` reaches the client as `UNKNOWN` rather than `NOT_FOUND`, and `ServiceUnavailableException` as `UNKNOWN` rather than `UNAVAILABLE`. A `DataAccessException` message can end up in the status description. `GlobalExceptionHandler` is `@RestControllerAdvice(basePackages = "dev.lmdb.ai.controller")`, so it covers the REST transport only.

The class Javadoc's claim of "one set of business logic, two transports" is true of the service layer and false of the validation and error-mapping layers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A request body failing a DTO constraint returns 400 naming the offending field, not 500
- [x] Malformed JSON, a missing required query parameter, and an over-limit upload each return 4xx, not 500
- [x] gRPC requests are validated before reaching the services, so a blank `message` is rejected rather than persisted as an empty turn
- [x] Business exceptions map to specific gRPC statuses (`NOT_FOUND`, `UNAVAILABLE`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`), never `UNKNOWN`, and no internal exception message reaches the status description
- [x] Each mapping above is covered by a test that fails if the mapping is removed
